full_judgment:
Under sections 21 to 23 of the Act, when the parties interested agree and apply for referring their difference in the suit to an agreed arbitrator at any time before the pronouncement of judgment, the Court is obliged to refer the matter in difference to the arbitrator and it shall specify in the order the time for making the award. After award was given, that must be filed in Court under section 14 and the Court is obliged thereupon to serve notice upon the parties of the filing of the award. Then, under section 17, if the Court finds no reason to remit the award or any matter in difference back to the arbitrator for reconsideration or does not set aside the award, the Court shall pronounce judgment but only after the expiration of the time for making an application to set aside the award or refusing the application if any made. Article 158 of the Limitation Act has provided a period of 30 days from the service of notice of filing of the award for making an application to set aside an award. A decree thereupon shall follow such judgment. But no appeal shall lie against such decree on the ground that the decree is in excess of or not exactly in accordance with the award. Under section 39, the orders against which an appeal shall lie have been enumerated. 

 14. Record shows that after receipt of the award on 8-8-1990, no notice was issued and/or served by the Court upon the parties of the filing of the award. Moreover, the Court pronounced the judgment before the expiration of the period for making an application to set aside the award as stated earlier. Section 17 of the Act however does not require of the Court to give any date for filing any objection to the award. If a party wants an award to be set aside on any of the grounds mentioned in section 30 of the Act, it must apply within 30 days of the date of service of notice of filing of the award as provided in article 158 of the Limitation Act. Pronouncing of the judgment under section 17 is made subject to the expiration of the period of 30 days from the date of service of the notice of filing of the award and this is a condition precedent to the exercise of the jurisdiction by the Court under the section. 

 "In view of the settled law and our discussion above, our answer to the question posed in the opening part of the judgment is that the period of the limitation for filing objections seeking the setting aside of an arbitration award commences from the date of service of the notice issued by the Court upon the parties regarding the filing of the award under section 14 (2) of the Act. Such a notice need not be in writing but what is essential is that the notice or intimation or communication of the filing of the award must be issued by the Court to the parties and served upon the parties concerned. Date of service of a notice issued by the arbitrator under section 14(1) of the Act or the date of obtaining an endorsement on the award by the arbitrator from the party concerned is irrelevant for determining the question of limitation for filing objections under Article 119 (b) of the Limitation Act, 1963 (Article 158 of Limitation Act, 1908)."
